chunks: He (Ayyub ibn Nuh) wrote to Abu al-Hassan (peace be upon him) asking him about God — Mighty and Majestic —

whether He knew the things before He created the things and brought them into being, or He did not know that until He created them and intended their creation and their coming into being, so He knew what He created at the time of creation, and what He brought into being at the time of bringing into being.
So he (the Imam) endorsed in his own handwriting: 'God never ceased to be Knowing of the things before He created the things, just as His knowledge of the things after He created the things.'

key_terms.تَكْوِين: Bringing into being, ontological origination — distinct from khalq (creation of form)
key_terms.عَالِماً: Knowing, the divine attribute of omniscience ('Ilm)
key_terms.فَوَقَّعَ بِخَطِّهِ: He endorsed/signed in his own handwriting — a tawqi', a brief written response by the Imam
key_terms.لَمْ يَزَلْ: Never ceased to be — indicates pre-eternal, unchanging divine attribute

ai.seo_question: Did God know things before He created them according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Ayyub ibn Nuh posed a crucial theological question to Imam al-Hadi (AS) through written correspondence about whether God's knowledge is pre-eternal or acquired at the moment of creation. The Imam's tawqi' (signed endorsement) decisively affirms that God's pre-eternal knowledge (al-'ilm al-azali) of all things is identical in nature to His knowledge after creation — there is no temporal change in divine knowledge. This hadith is foundational for Shia theology's position on divine attributes and refutes any notion that God's knowledge is dependent on or caused by creation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Sa’ad Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, 
‘He wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic,

‘Did He<sup>azwj</sup> Know of the things before He<sup>azwj</sup> Created the things and their occurrence (coming into being), or did He<sup>azwj</sup> not Know that until He<sup>azwj</sup> Created these and Intended their Creation and their coming into being, So He<sup>azwj</sup> Knew what He<sup>azwj</sup> Created during what He<sup>azwj</sup> Created, and what is to come into being during what came into being’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> signed: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> never ceased to be Knowing of the thing before He<sup>azwj</sup> Created the things, just like His<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge of the things after having Created the things’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Sa‘d ibn ‘Abdallah from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ayyub ibn Nuh, who wrote to abu al-Hassan (al-Thalith (a.s.) asking him about Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious.

“Did He know all things before creating and giving them being, or did He not know until He brought them into existence or until He willed their creation and existence? Did Allah come to know what He created during the process of their creation and what He originated during their being originated?”
The Imam wrote in reply in his own handwriting, “Eternally Allah has had full knowledge of all things, before as well as after their creation.”
